paper.title: Stay Within Your Bounds: Distance-Guided Decoding for Guaranteed Context-Free Grammar Compliance

read: full text (arXiv HTML): Sections 1, 3-6, Limitations and Appendices A-C (system, ablations, budget saturation); D (worked example) skimmed; Section 2 related work skimmed

claims.claim: Constrained decoding that only keeps each prefix extendable to some valid string can still fail to finish a valid output within a finite token budget, especially when the model's subword tokens do not line up with the grammar's terminals; precomputing, for a bounded-stack summary of the grammar's pushdown automaton, an upper bound on how many tokens are still needed to reach acceptance, and pruning any continuation whose bound exceeds the remaining budget, guarantees that every returned output is grammatical. Supported only if, with a 120-token budget, the decoder produces 100% syntactically valid outputs on JSON, SQL and linear temporal logic for all three base models tested and 100% schema-valid JSON, while every prefix-masking decoder (Guidance, Outlines, XGrammar, SynCode) and sequential Monte Carlo steering stay below 100% schema validity on every model even with budgets raised to 4,096 tokens; and if its JSON decoding is faster than sampling ten outputs and filtering for validity.
claims.decision_rule: Syn = 100% on JSON/SQL/LTL x 3 models; JSON schema = 100% on 3 models; all baselines < 100% schema at T in {512..4096}; SWYB JSON time < Sample-Verify time.

claims.claim: Grammar-guaranteed decoding with this lookahead also produces semantically better structured outputs than other constrained or unconstrained decoders, because beam search over model and automaton-proposed tokens avoids being forced onto low-probability repair tokens, and promoting tokens that reduce the distance to acceptance adds further gains. Supported only if it has the highest SQL execution accuracy on Spider and the highest formula-equivalence accuracy on drone-planning temporal logic for each of three base models, and if, with beam search held fixed, adding distance-guided scoring raises accuracy in all six model-task pairs.
claims.decision_rule: SWYB best Ex. (Spider) and Acc. (LTL) on all 3 models; DGS+4 beams > no-DGS+4 beams on all 6 pairs.

experiments.text: Define the decoder. Setup: translate the grammar to a pushdown automaton; offline, compute bounded-stack summaries (stack height H) with Pre*-style reachability and, by weighting each terminal with the minimum number of model tokens needed to emit it, an upper bound on the token distance to acceptance. Online, track configurations including a partially matched terminal so subword tokens can cross terminal boundaries; combine the model's top-k tokens with automaton-proposed tokens, keep only those whose successors can still reach acceptance within the remaining budget, push the logits of tokens that make progress towards acceptance toward the best viable logit (strength alpha), and run beam search; configurations missing from the cache are computed on the fly. A theorem shows every returned output is accepted and one is returned whenever the bound fits the budget. Preprocessing takes 0.29 s for schema-specific JSON grammars, 0.42 s for LTL (H = 50) and 3 h 40 min for SQL (H = 13).

Fix the benchmarks and baselines. Setup: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; json-mode-eval (100 schema-conditioned JSON examples), Spider validation (1,034 text-to-SQL), and the drone-planning LTL golden set (6,185); token budget 120 for all. Baselines: the unconstrained model (temperature 0.8, 10 seeds), sample-and-verify over those 10 samples, Guidance, Outlines, XGrammar, SynCode (strict) and GenLM sequential Monte Carlo (2 or 5 particles) where their public code supports the grammar; XGrammar dropped for SQL at about 20 s per token; no baseline supports LTL natively except SynCode. Metrics: syntactic validity, JSON schema validity, SQL execution accuracy, LTL accuracy by Buchi-automaton equivalence, perplexity under the base model, and seconds per output.

Generate JSON. Result: syntactic / schema validity 100 / 100% on all three models, against at best 96 / 90% (Llama-3.1-8B; Guidance and Outlines), 95 / 90% (Llama-3.2-3B; XGrammar, Outlines) and 96 / 89% (Qwen2.5-7B; sample-and-verify, Outlines, GenLM); unconstrained 63.7 / 57.1, 56.4 / 49.4 and 93.6 / 87.4%. Time 3.46-4.05 s per output, against 9.65-17.38 s for sample-and-verify and 0.96-3.62 s for masking decoders; perplexity 1.11-1.14 against 1.01-1.08 for most baselines and 1.38-1.80 for XGrammar.

Check whether local decoders just need more tokens. Setup: rerun JSON with budgets 512, 1,024, 2,048 and 4,096 for Guidance, Outlines, SynCode and GenLM. Result: syntactic validity reaches 95-100% but schema validity stays at 79-93% for every method and model, essentially flat across budgets (e.g. SynCode 83% on Llama-3.1-8B at every budget while its time grows from 13.27 to 113.81 s); the authors attribute this to local decoders opening nested structures without a signal to close them.

Note what makes JSON schema validity attainable. Setup: the decoder is given a grammar compiled from each example's schema, so grammatical acceptance implies schema validity, whereas baselines use their own schema support; deterministic decoders are reported from a single run; the sample-and-verify baseline draws only 10 samples per input. The guarantee also holds only when the bounded summary certifies a completion within the budget; otherwise the decoder reports failure instead of an output.

Generate SQL and temporal logic. Result: Spider execution accuracy 61.1 / 51.5 / 62.8% (Llama-3.1-8B / Llama-3.2-3B / Qwen2.5-7B) against 59.2 / 49.4 / 51.9% for GenLM, 57.5 / 47.8 / 61.5% for sample-and-verify, 43.2 / 39.6 / 43.2% for SynCode and 53.8 / 46.3 / 61.4% unconstrained; time 9.92 / 6.25 / 13.03 s against 8.90 / 5.29 / 8.83 s for sample-and-verify. LTL accuracy 29.6 / 22.1 / 31.6% against 24.4 / 15.2 / 31.0% for SynCode and 22.1 / 9.6 / 30.9% unconstrained. Margins over the best baseline are 1.3-2.1 points on SQL and 0.6-6.9 on LTL.

Ablate beam search and distance-guided scoring. Setup: SQL and LTL, each model, with or without 4-beam search and with or without distance-guided scoring (alpha = 0.5). Result: SQL execution without either 26.0 / 22.1 / 22.2% (Llama-3.2-3B / Llama-3.1-8B / Qwen), with beams only 50.9 / 60.4 / 61.6%, with both 51.2 / 60.9 / 62.8%; LTL 16.5 / 29.2 / 30.5% without either, 21.8 / 29.4 / 31.2% with beams, 22.1 / 29.6 / 31.6% with both; distance scoring without beams lowers LTL on Llama-3.1-8B to 24.9%. Syntactic validity is 100% in every configuration. Without beams the decoder falls back to the automaton's highest-probability token whenever the model's single proposal is invalid, which hurts quality.

Note tuning and reporting details. Setup: the scoring strength alpha is chosen per model and task (0.25-0.75), and the main-table SQL numbers differ slightly from the ablation's alpha = 0.5 row; baselines use default settings. The SynCode SQL row for Qwen2.5-7B is identical to its Llama-3.1-8B row in every column, which may be a reporting error.

notes: Drafted from scratch from arXiv HTML for the dataset50 rebuild, without consulting earlier claims or references. The c1 distance-scoring bar is the paper's 'smaller but consistent improvements' made checkable: with 4 beams the gains are +0.3/+0.5/+1.2 (SQL) and +0.3/+0.2/+0.4 (LTL). The JSON schema-grammar point in the c0 confound is from the preprocessing paragraph ('schema-specific JSON grammars'); how the baselines are given schemas is not described.
